correctness.rationale: With B=1-1_{no *} and P(no *)=s^n, Cov(B,K)=s^n[E K-E(K|no *)] holds. Conditional residual observations are iid t and give F(s)=1-s^n+sum((1-t_i)^n-(1-st_i)^n). Its second derivative equals -n(n-1)[s^{n-2}+sum t_i^2(1-st_i)^{n-2}]<0. F(0)=1-E_t K_n<0 for n>=2 and r>=2 positive t; F(1)=0; F′(1)<0. Strict concavity produces exactly one interior zero, with signs negative then positive. The limit H(x)=1-sum exp(-xt_i) has a unique positive root and positive derivative, so the O(1/n) Taylor correction in F(x/n) gives the stated negative second coefficient and O_t(n^-3) in sigma. For n>=r+1 and s<sigma, the conditional mean of K given B=1 is smaller than when B=0; yet K=r+1 has positive probability given B=1 and is impossible given B=0. Thus neither conditional law FOSD-dominates. Independently enumerated 76 exact rational cases (4 profiles, n=2..6 or 5, 4 s choices), also checked sigma_2=1/3, and ran 4 high-precision root profiles at n=100,500,2000 confirming the second-order coefficient. No finite test substituted for the analytic all-parameter argument.
residual_risks: The two-term O_t(n^-3) expansion fixes the strictly positive t profile; no uniformity is claimed when t_i tends to zero or r grows with n.
The proof establishes first-order stochastic incomparability only for s<sigma and n>=r+1; it gives no likelihood-ratio/negative-association classification beyond that regime.
Tests are bounded; the all-n statement depends on exact conditional expectation and strict concavity, not on checking finite cases.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge PASS for the global unique concentration-path sign transition, its fixed-profile Poisson-scale second coefficient and the conditional first-order stochastic-incomparability regime. Prior occupied-box indicator covariance identities already imply the raw finite Cov(B,K) expression, which is not a new identity. Their pairwise anti-correlation and positive inverse do not mathematically force the row-sum sign or its unique parameter switch. The published equal-box richness--frequency-count switch changes a frequency index instead of distinguished-cell mass. Bogachev--Gnedin--Yakubovich 2006 supplies the cross terms in the variance of the occupied-box count and pursues infinite-box asymptotics, not the present finite-species one-parameter threshold. Complete arXiv 2022 missing-mass paper studies estimator risk, Fisher scoring and bounds, not this conditional covariance. A highly relevant 2009 ecological occurrence/richness study remains full-text inaccessible: its spatial site-incidence design is distinguishable in abstract but the whole-document priority implication is not ruled out. Searches did not expose exact prior dominating theorem; remaining risk is explicitly preserved.
residual_risks: Sizling et al. 2009 full paper was inaccessible even after preprint/OA and authorized Oxford routes; an equivalent result in its appendices is a live but not dispositive priority risk.
Unindexed older fixed-sample urn/occupancy texts might give the same concavity argument or asymptotic root under alternative notation.
The raw covariance identity is known from the occupied-indicator matrix and is not an independent originality contribution.
The exact phase theorem is only along a fixed residual profile and does not imply a sign classification for arbitrary curves in the simplex.

value.rationale: Covariance between a particular species being observed and total observed species richness is an interpretable natural indicator in occupancy/ecology: the direct positive contribution of that species competes with negative cross-occupancy correlations. The sharp finite-n one-switch theorem resolves which mechanism wins along any fixed heterogeneous conditional community profile; the Poisson-scale root and explicit second coefficient describe when a rare distinguished species crosses the boundary as sample size grows. Conditional richness distributions can lack even first-order stochastic ordering despite a definite mean sign, giving a meaningful methodological boundary. These precise mathematical facts are not known table recomputation nor a renaming of pairwise covariances, although the raw identity is earlier work. No general ecological causality or empirical dataset claim is made.
residual_risks: Interpretation is specific to iid finite multinomial sampling, not spatial ecological causation or arbitrary non-iid abundance mechanisms.
The exact critical root may be computationally implicit for heterogeneous profiles, and no uniform growing-category asymptotic is established.

limitations: The inspected prior row-sum covariance formula itself is not new.
2009 Sizling et al. full text unavailable after arXiv/OA/authorized Oxford attempts; only abstract was read and implicit historical coverage is a residual risk.
No assertive publication guard or complete confidentiality-clean replacements for METADATA.json/AUDIT.json were staged, so publication remains not_ready.
Mathematical results are restricted to fixed r and strictly positive fixed t for the asymptotics; finite checks are not universal certification.
